limitations: WHO cumulative counts and the provincial 21-day series are as of 17 November; the 20 November publication date is not a synchronized epidemiological snapshot.
Africa CDC's 11% case-identification-from-contact-lists measure and WHO's 81% daily contact-follow-up measure use different denominators and observation periods.
Security incidents and casualties remain attributed to WHO and partner statements; no independent incident-level verification is claimed.
The regional map uses country-status cards rather than geographic coordinates and preserves the different observation dates.
The Swiss medical-evacuation patient's occupation is not specified in the cited WHO notice.

issues.evidence: The 20 November WHO Disease Outbreak News identifies the 26 October Switzerland evacuation as a case treated in Geneva and discharged on 11 November, without identifying the patient's occupation. The same notice explicitly identifies the person discharged in the United Kingdom on 18 November as a medically evacuated health and care worker. The staged sentence classifies both evacuated patients as health workers, which is unsupported for the Swiss case. In addition, the sentence that the third Committee meeting 'did not issue a new pandemic-emergency classification' makes a negative claim not stated in the 20 November notice. The direct 17 May WHO statement supports the original Director-General determination; the 20 November notice records the subsequent PHEIC reaffirmation, not a new pandemic-emergency ruling. Sources: https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON630 and https://www.who.int/news/item/17-05-2026-epidemic-of-ebola-disease-in-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-and-uganda-determined-a-public-health-emergency-of-international-concern.
